Feed instances whenever available; procedure stops first instance produces declaration refuses data , pre-registered protocol ends :
code: set.seed(42) simulate_batch <- function(instances, mu = 0.05, sd = 0.10) {   h <- sd * sqrt(3)   la <- runif(length(instances), 0.4, 0.8)   data.frame(instance = instances, seed = 1L,              loss_a = la, loss_b = la - mu + runif(length(instances), -h, h)) }  state <- initialize_comparison(design) state <- update_comparison(state, simulate_batch(1:50)) state #>  #> ── seqbench comparison ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Boundary betting, alpha = 0.05, margin = 0.02, bounds [0, 1] #> • Instances: 50, evaluations: 50, cost: 50 / 800 #> • Estimate of mean(loss_a - loss_b): 0.068 #> • Confidence sequence (running intersection): [-0.07653, 0.1935] #> • Decision: continue sampling state <- update_comparison(state, simulate_batch(51:400)) #> Warning: Stopped at instance "206" (t = 206) with decision "B"; 194 later instances were #> not consumed. #> ℹ Under the pre-registered protocol the experiment ends here. stopping_decision(state) #> [1] "B" #> attr(,"reason") #> [1] "declaration"

title: Anytime-Valid Sequential Benchmarking of Algorithms
text: Anytime-valid sequential benchmarking algorithms. seqbench answers one question: can stop comparing algorithm algorithm B without invalidating inference? treats benchmark sequential experiment paired losses (instance, seed) maintains confidence sequence mean paired difference stays valid optional stopping, repeated inspection adaptive budgets. Three declarations possible, relative pre-registered margin practical relevance δ:

title: Anytime-Valid Sequential Benchmarking of Algorithms
text: Version 0.1.0, first release; API experimental may change minor releases. Implemented: five boundaries (betting, empirical Bernstein, Hoeffding, Bernstein declared variance bound, invalid fixed-sample negative control), instance-level updating seeds clusters, three-way decision rule, budget accounting, print, summary, tidy, glance autoplot methods. Instances sequential unit; several seeds instance averaged one observation. Losses outside bounds, missing values instances reappear losses seen errors, never silently converted.
code: library(seqbench)  design <- comparison_design(alpha = 0.05, margin = 0.02, bounds = c(0, 1),                             boundary = "betting", budget = 500) state  <- initialize_comparison(design)  # paired losses: one row per (instance, seed); losses within `bounds` losses <- data.frame(instance = 1:40, seed = 1,                      loss_a = runif(40, 0.1, 0.4), loss_b = runif(40, 0.3, 0.6)) state  <- update_comparison(state, losses)  stopping_decision(state)     # "A", "B", "equivalent", "continue" or "inconclusive" comparison_report(state)     # estimand, estimate, C_t, assumptions, cost, seeds, versions tidy(state)                  # trajectory, one row per instance ggplot2::autoplot(state)     # C_t against t with the [-margin, margin] band

text: New boundary "bernstein_declared": predictable-plug-Bennett confidence sequence declared upper bound sd_max standard deviation paired difference (assumption A5, recorded report). Valid declared bound holds; gain betting modest Bennett range term keeps log(2/alpha)/t floor bounded observations.

title: seqbench 0.0.0.9001
text: Betting boundary: endpoint refinement bisection now lazy inside update_comparison() (decision threshold falls boundary grid cell, plus per call reporting). Decisions stopping times unchanged; per-instance cost now linear grid size instead linear number observations (2000-instance stream margin went minutes 0.3 s). boundary_interval() gained thresholds argument. Betting boundary: nonempty confidence set narrower one grid cell now located searching exact capital instead reported empty (found external review; constant streams triggered ). update_comparison() re-evaluates decision final endpoint refinement, empty running intersection always reported . planning_horizon() honours max_t; n_max, betting_grid refine validated whole numbers / logical; costs must finite.
